subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask — GPU price protection language
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Robotics Procurement <procurement@acme.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity ask — concern on GPU pricing volatility

Soojin,

Thanks for the demo last week — the Redwood Dedicated perf looked great. Were ready to put a reservation in for Q3 (targeting 1.2k A100-equivalent GPU hours / month; 12 month term), but procurement raised a concern: with new hardware and falling spot/wholesale GPU prices, we dont want to commit to a headline discount that could become punitive if costs drop materially.

Would Redwood consider a price-protection clause or an indexation approach so that our committed unit price can step with a published GPU index? If not indexation, is there a tranche-based guarantee or floor/ceiling you can offer? Wed like to avoid huge manual renegotiations mid-term.

If you can share a draft term sheet with the proposed language and any attachment/spec on the index, well fast-track procurement review.

Thanks,
Tom Reynolds
Head of Cloud Procurement | Acme Robotics
Tom.Reynolds@acme.ai

--

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme.ai>
Cc: Acme Robotics Procurement <procurement@acme.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask — concern on GPU pricing volatility

Tom,

Really appreciate the clear ask and the context from procurement. We can absolutely support a mechanism to share GPU price movement risk — our aim is to make reserved commitments safe for both sides without constant renegotiation. Ive attached a draft term sheet (Acme_TermSheet_v3.pdf) and a short spec for a GPU Price Index (gpu-price-index-spec.xlsx) that we use internally. High level proposal below:

- Term: 12 months with an optional 3-month ramp (first 3 months billed at 60% commit level)
- Capacity: baseline 1.2k A100-equivalent GPU-hours / month, monthly true-up
- Pricing: tiered committed discount (5/10/15/20%) by monthly utilization bands; headline discount is applied to Redwood list rate
- GPU Price Index adjustment: quarterly reconciliation using a third-party GPU wholesale index (we propose NVIDIA Wholesale Index v1 — see spec). If index moves down >10% vs contract benchmark, customer can elect either (a) a one-time step-down in unit rate capped at -6% per quarter, or (b) an agreed credit applied to next invoice. If index moves up >12%, Redwood can apply an upward adjustment capped at +4% per quarter. Net exposure limited by floor/ceiling.
- Approval & governance: discounts >18% need finance + VP sign-off; any index-driven adjustment >5% will trigger a notification window and a required exec sign-off for both sides.

Attachments included: Acme_TermSheet_v3.pdf, gpu-price-index-spec.xlsx, and a short clause draft well circulate for legal. This keeps things automated (index math) but safe (caps & notification).

If that looks directionally good, can we schedule a 30-min call tomorrow to walk procurement through the index spec and the reconciliation cadence?

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Exec, Strategic Sales | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Attachments: Acme_TermSheet_v3.pdf; gpu-price-index-spec.xlsx

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask — concern on GPU pricing volatility

Looping in finance notes on the index proposal. Were supportive of an indexation approach in principle but recommend:

- Floor/ceiling assumptions be explicit in the term sheet (we should propose a -8% floor and +6% ceiling across the 12-month period, then revisit at renewal).
- Cap the index-driven downward pass-through to avoid negative margin scenarios; suggest the -6% cap per quarter (as Soojin suggested) but add an annual cumulative cap of -10%.
- For discounts >15% at any tier, require credit committee visibility; discounts >20% should route to VP of Finance for approval (this is non-negotiable for us).
- Require that the index source and methodology be immutable for the term (documented in gpu-price-index-spec.xlsx) or change only by mutual written consent.

I attached a short cost-sensitivity table I ran (see gpu-price-index-spec.xlsx tab "sensitivity"). If procurement wants an explicit insurance-like rider (third-party hedge), thats possible but would add premium — we should flag that to the customer.

Marcus
Director, Revenue Finance | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: gpu-price-index-spec.xlsx

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask — concern on GPU pricing volatility

Soojin / Marcus,

From an approvals and ops standpoint, I recommend the following operational guardrails to keep this manageable:

- Any price adjustment requires 14 calendar days notice before the next invoice cycle.
- Create an "index reconciliation" invoice line item to keep transparency in billing (shows baseline price, index adjustment, net).
- Add CLARITY in the term sheet that utilization true-ups are monthly and cannot be netted across quarters for index adjustments.
- For contract amendments (index > threshold and either party requests a re-work), we auto-scope an internal 7-business-day review SLA.

Ive started a draft clause for legal to slot into the term sheet (draft_clause_gpu_index.docx). Also — approvals: discounts up to 15% are Sales Leader approve, 15-20% Director + Finance, >20% require VP. That aligns with Marcus but Ill need e-approval routing set up in CLM if Tom accepts.

Laura Bennett
Head, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Tom — thanks for raising this. Quick summary / proposed next steps so we can close the commercial: 

1) Redwood provides 12-month reserved capacity for 1.2k A100-equivalent GPU-hours / month with a 3-month ramp.
2) Pricing uses a tiered committed discount matrix; discounts are subject to approval thresholds (Sales Leader / Director / VP per Laura).
3) GPU Price Index reconciliation: quarterly measurements against the NVIDIA Wholesale Index v1. Downward moves >10% from benchmark trigger a customer election: one-time step-down capped at -6%/quarter (annual cumulative cap -10%), or invoice credit. Upward moves >12% can trigger +4%/quarter (with notification). Index mechanics and immutable source documented in gpu-price-index-spec.xlsx.
4) Ops: 14-day notice window for adjustments, reconciliation line item on invoice, monthly true-ups.

Ive attached the term sheet and spec. If Acme procurement is comfortable, please confirm acceptance of the term sheet by reply and well issue a formal DocuSign package (link below) and schedule a 30-min call to walk through the reconciliation mechanics. If you want us to soften caps or remove auto-upwards for your internal approval, say so and well model the finance impact.

Proposed call times (PT): Thu 13 May 09:00 or 15:00 — which works for you?

Thanks,
Soojin
